# 0003 — The traceability matrix is generated by the build, not written by hand

- **Status:** accepted
- **Date:** 2026-09-05
- **Manuscript:** §11, Decision 11-A; §13

## Context

"Automated Verification of Requirements" is an explicit section of the brief, wanting test
cases, validation rules, CI/CD quality gates and verification reports. The usual response is a
table in the report mapping requirements to tests. Such a table is accurate on the day it is
typed and drifts every day after.

## Decision

`docs/requirements.md` is the single source of truth for FR, NFR and architecture rules. Tests
claim coverage by annotating themselves:

```java
@Test
@Requirement("FR-06")
void unknownTokenAndUnknownCredentialAreIndistinguishable() { ... }
```

The Gradle task `traceabilityReport` parses the register, scans both test source sets for the
annotations, writes the matrix to `build/reports/traceability/traceability.md`, posts it as a
pull-request comment, and **fails the build** when a requirement marked `required` has no
covering test. It also fails when an annotation names an id that is not in the register, which
catches typos that would otherwise silently claim coverage.

## Rejected alternatives

**A hand-maintained table in the report.** Cannot drift-check itself, and a marker has no way
to distinguish a true row from an aspirational one.

**Deriving coverage from JaCoCo alone.** Coverage says which lines ran, not which requirement
was verified. A test can execute the verification path and assert nothing about the requirement.

## Consequences

- Three statuses rather than two. `required` must have a test. `planned` is legitimate
  mid-project and prints a warning — an honest partial reads better than an implausible green.
  `gate` marks requirements enforced by a pipeline stage (coverage, static analysis, CVE
  scanning) rather than by a test case.
- Moving a requirement from `planned` to `required` is a deliberate, reviewable commit. That
  transition is the definition of done for a feature issue.
- The matrix in the report carries a commit SHA and a run number, so it is evidence rather
  than description.
